symmetryCheck: Control: apply the 'investigation opened, what happened' lens to BJP-aligned business/political figures with no theory in hand. Result: Gali Janardhana Reddy (BJP MLA) was convicted and sentenced to 7 years on 6 May 2025 — but the case was registered in Dec 2009 under Congress governments and took 15 years; MEIL (Rs 584 crore to BJP) was booked by CBI on 31 Mar 2024 — but no charge sheet is traceable 30 months later; Aurobindo's director was arrested by ED (Nov 2022) — then became the prosecution's approver while his company donated Rs 30 crore to BJP; Adani faced 24 SEBI investigations, an SC-monitored process and a US indictment — the public Indian closures are no-violation orders and a Rs 1.51 crore settlement, and the US case was dismissed on DOJ's own motion. Opposition control: Hemant Soren (JMM) was arrested and jailed five months, then bailed with the HC finding reasons to believe he was not guilty and the SC dismissing ED's appeal; the Chhattisgarh CMO officer was jailed ~2.5 years before SC interim bail; Tamil Nadu's IAS collectors were summoned en masse and the SC backed ED, yet no case has been filed. The lens produces alarming pictures on both sides: on the ruling-party side the pattern is 'booked but not prosecuted'; on the opposition side it is 'jailed then bailed without trial'. Conclusion about the lens: 'was an investigation opened' does not discriminate; 'did it reach a charge sheet or verdict, and how long did custody last' does. The only verdict in this file (Janardhana Reddy) went against a BJP-aligned figure, which is a genuine counter-datum, tempered by its 2009 origin.
